$note: One corpus, two implementations. The editor validates in TypeScript (@reeve-iot/workflow-core) to tell an
author what is wrong; the backend compiles in C# to refuse to publish or start what the run would not
execute as drawn. They are separate code in separate languages and they drift. This file grades both.
VERDICT is graded on every case, on both sides. A side `gradedBy` lists must reach the case's verdict: if
one listed side calls a definition valid and another rejects it, that is a defect on one of them, never a
difference of opinion. A side it leaves out must call the definition valid, since a side is left out only
for a rule it does not implement. RULE identity is graded on each side a case lists: that side must report
one of the case's `rules`, ids of contracts/rule-parity.json, which an invalid case names and a valid one
does not. Message TEXT is graded nowhere — see exemptions.
`gradedBy` names each side that grades a case. A side it leaves out is a key of `notGradedBy`, whose value
says why, so its silence is recorded rather than implied. Both harnesses run every case, so a marker that
goes stale fails too. A case holds no key but name, why, gradedBy, notGradedBy, signature, definition and
expect, and `expect` none but verdict and rules; the backend harness refuses any other rather than ignore it.
The marker follows from the rules a case expects: the backend is always listed, and the editor exactly when
the case is valid or every rule it expects is one rule-parity.json classes editor. So a case cannot record
a rule the editor grades only in part (a `part` in rule-parity.json), nor a finding the editor alone reports.
The definition shape is the editor's ({nodes, edges}). The backend reads it with StoredWorkflowDocument.Read,
which matches keys exactly and refuses a key it does not list, so one document loads
on both sides by the same keys, without a translation layer that could itself drift. `blocks` is the
catalogue both sides grade against; `signature`, where a case has one, holds the workflow's stored input and
output parameter lists.
The backend harness reads a case as the compilation service reads a stored version: the definition text
through StoredWorkflowDocument.Read, the parameter lists through CanvasSignature.TryRead, then
WorkflowCompiler.Compile, whose structure phase runs the run's own ValidateRootCanvas and TopologicalSort.
The editor harness grades validateStructureFindings on the document as held and the store's
validateWorkflowFindings with the document loaded; both read each finding's rule id.
Each case pins one rule, with its reason; not every rule-parity.json id has a case here. The generated
matrices both halves grade exactly are contracts/rule-agreement.json (the rules whose rule-parity.json row
names it, at each depth; graded by RuleAgreementTests and ruleAgreement.test.ts) and
contracts/dangling-edge-agreement.json (a wire naming a missing node, by depth, end and mapping kind; graded
by DanglingEdgeAgreementTests and danglingEdgeAgreement.test.ts).
Harnesses: dotnet/tests/ReeveWorkflow.Core.Tests/Model/WorkflowValidationCorpusTests.cs and
packages/core/src/editor/validationCorpus.test.ts

exemptions.reason: Already drifted and harmlessly so: the backend says 'Workflow contains a cycle.' and the editor 'Workflow contains a cycle'. Grading text would fail on a full stop, get weakened, and end up proving nothing.

The backend's root structure check stops at the FIRST broken rule because it only has to refuse; the editor collects every finding because its job is to show an author the whole list. A corpus demanding equal counts would be demanding the editor stop being useful.

cases.name: empty-graph
cases.why: A canvas with nothing on it is not an error; both sides return before any rule runs.

cases.name: minimal-valid
cases.why: The smallest thing that must pass: one start node and one node wired to it.

cases.name: no-start-node
cases.why: Nodes exist but nothing says where execution begins.

cases.name: extra-root
cases.why: A second entry point. Execution would have to guess which one starts the run.

cases.name: cycle
cases.why: Every node has an incoming edge, so only acyclicity catches this.

cases.name: disconnected-cycle-island
cases.why: A two-node cycle off to the side. Both nodes have an incoming edge, so it is not an extra root. Both sides reach the unreachability rule first — the backend throws there and the editor lists it before the cycle — so this pins 'unreachable', not either-of-two.

cases.name: input-has-incoming
cases.why: Something wires back into the start node. Its source has no incoming edge either, and both sides name the start node's rule for it.

cases.name: duplicate-input-mapping
cases.why: Two parents map the same input on one node. Single start, everything reachable, acyclic — this is the only rule that can refuse it, and it is the rule the corpus had no case for.

cases.name: duplicate-edge-pair
cases.why: Two wires join one source and one target. Single start, everything reachable, acyclic, no input mapped twice: only the pair rule refuses it.

cases.name: required-input-unfed
cases.why: A required input nothing feeds: no mapping, no configured value. The run would hand the block nothing where it declared it needs a value.

cases.name: wire-port-unknown
cases.why: A mapping reads an output its source does not have. The run finds nothing under that name for the input.

cases.name: wire-port-unknown-root-output-mapping
cases.why: A wire into the exit node writes 'result', and the workflow declares only 'Result': the run writes the name anyway, as any wire into the exit node naming it.

cases.name: root-output-mapping-declared
cases.why: The same wire, with 'result' among the workflow's declared outputs.

cases.name: declared-output-shadows-static
cases.why: A node declares an output under the name of one its block already has, so one name would stand for two ports.

cases.name: port-type-mismatch
cases.why: A Number output wired into a Boolean input; the widening table has no path from one to the other. The run hands the Boolean input the number unconverted.

notGradedBy.editor: rule-parity.json classes port-type-mismatch compiler-only: the editor does not implement it, and calls this definition valid.

cases.name: expression-syntax
cases.why: An expression the expression language cannot parse.

notGradedBy.editor: rule-parity.json classes expression-syntax compiler-only: the editor does not implement it, and calls this definition valid.

cases.name: expression-out-of-scope
cases.why: A node inside a loop body reads a node on the parent canvas. It looks legal, but the body's run sees only the outputs of its own canvas, so the reference evaluates to null without a word.

notGradedBy.editor: rule-parity.json classes expression-out-of-scope compiler-only: the editor does not implement it, and calls this definition valid.

cases.name: declared-output-type-null-corpus
cases.why: The declared-output type is null; the reader and compiler refuse malformed port types.

cases.name: declared-output-type-absent-corpus
cases.why: The declared-output type is absent; the reader and compiler refuse malformed port types.

cases.name: parameter-type-null-corpus
cases.why: The parameter type is null; the reader and compiler refuse malformed port types.

cases.name: parameter-type-absent-corpus
cases.why: The parameter type is absent; the reader and compiler refuse malformed port types.

cases.name: port-entry-type-null-corpus
cases.why: The port-entry type is null; the reader and compiler refuse malformed port types.

cases.name: port-entry-type-absent-corpus
cases.why: The port-entry type is absent; the reader and compiler refuse malformed port types.

cases.name: type-parameter-unbound-absent-literal-corpus
cases.why: The registered Filter's Collection<$T> is fed a literal with no literalValue, which gives no evidence, so the literal needs a T that nothing binds.

notGradedBy.editor: type-parameter-unbound is compiler-only; the editor does not grade compiler rules.

cases.name: type-parameter-conflict-mixed-literal-corpus
cases.why: The registered Filter's Collection<$T> is fed the literal [1, "a"]: T >= Int and T >= String have no least upper bound.

notGradedBy.editor: type-parameter-conflict is compiler-only; the editor does not grade compiler rules.

cases.name: port-type-malformed-dynamic-output
cases.why: A dynamic output typed CollectionFoo on a block with dynamic ports: a spelling the grammar refuses.

cases.name: port-type-malformed-parameter
cases.why: A workflow input parameter with no type.

cases.name: port-type-malformed-output-parameter
cases.why: A workflow output parameter whose type never closes its angle bracket: the stored output list is read on both sides.

cases.name: port-type-malformed-declared-output
cases.why: A declared output typed Collection<Foo, its bracket never closed.

cases.name: sub-canvas-valid
cases.why: A loop body reads the branch input its block declares and a name its container passes through, both wired from the body's entry node. The body's signature is the two together.

cases.name: sub-canvas-name-unknown
cases.why: A node holds a branch under a name its block never declares.

cases.name: edge-endpoint-unknown
cases.why: A wire names a source node that is not on the canvas. The run cannot deliver anything along it.

cases.name: edge-endpoint-unknown-in-sub-canvas
cases.why: Inside a loop body, a wire names a target node that is not on the body's canvas: the root-only structure rules stop there and this one still holds.

cases.name: declared-output-type-alias-corpus
cases.why: The declared-output type is spelled by an alias of a registered type; the compile refuses it.

notGradedBy.editor: port-type-alias is compiler-only; the editor does not grade compiler rules.

cases.name: port-entry-type-alias-corpus
cases.why: The port-entry type is spelled by an alias of a registered type; the compile refuses it.

notGradedBy.editor: port-type-alias is compiler-only; the editor does not grade compiler rules.

cases.name: parameter-type-alias-corpus
cases.why: The parameter type is spelled by an alias of a registered type; the compile refuses it.

notGradedBy.editor: port-type-alias is compiler-only; the editor does not grade compiler rules.

cases.name: declared-output-type-unregistered-corpus
cases.why: The declared-output type names no type the host's vocabulary registers; the compile refuses it.

notGradedBy.editor: port-type-unregistered is compiler-only; the editor does not grade compiler rules.

cases.name: port-entry-type-unregistered-corpus
cases.why: The port-entry type names no type the host's vocabulary registers; the compile refuses it.

notGradedBy.editor: port-type-unregistered is compiler-only; the editor does not grade compiler rules.

cases.name: parameter-type-unregistered-corpus
cases.why: The parameter type names no type the host's vocabulary registers; the compile refuses it.

notGradedBy.editor: port-type-unregistered is compiler-only; the editor does not grade compiler rules.

cases.name: port-list-without-dynamic-ports
cases.why: A port list sits in the configuration of a block that declares no dynamic ports; the run reads no such list.

cases.name: declared-outputs-unsupported
cases.why: A node declares an output and its block supports no declared outputs, so the editor offers none there.

cases.name: port-list-on-entry-node
cases.why: The library's entry node declares no dynamic ports, so a port list in its configuration is read by nothing; the editor grades it as the compile does.

cases.name: declared-outputs-on-exit-node
cases.why: The library's exit node supports no declared outputs, so one declared on it is read by nothing; the editor grades it as the compile does.

cases.name: declared-output-source-unknown
cases.why: A declared output takes its source from a key that is no sub-canvas of its block.
